message.content:
Here are some of the most popular books written by J.K. Rowling:

| Title | Year Published | Notes |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** (also *Sorcerer’s Stone* in the U.S.) | 1997 | The first book in the Harry Potter series; introduced the world of Hogwarts. |
| **Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets** | 1998 | Continues Harry’s adventures and introduces the Chamber of Secrets plot. |
| **Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban** | 1999 | Adds the character Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map. |
| **Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire** | 2000 | Features the Triwizard Tournament and the return of Voldemort. |
| **Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix** | 2003 | Introduces Dumbledore’s Army and the Ministry of Magic’s interference. |
| **Harry Potter and the Half‑Blood Prince** | 2005 | Explores Voldemort’s backstory and the concept of Horcruxes. |
| **Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows** | 2007 | Concludes the series with the final battle at Hogwarts. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel, dealing with political intrigue in a small town. |
| **The Cuckoo’s Calling** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2013 | A crime thriller featuring private detective Cormoran Strike. |
| **The Silkworm** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2014 | Continues the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Career of Evil** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2015 | Another entry in the Strike series. |
| **Lethal White** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2018 | The fifth book in the Cormoran Strike saga. |
| **The Ickabog** | 2020 | A children’s fable published as a free e‑book during the COVID‑19 pandemic. |

These titles have been bestsellers worldwide and have garnered a massive fan base across all age groups.
